text: resident firstboot: seed the intent log from /usr/lib/resident/intents.json so every package, service and config file in the image has a recorded reason (resident-firstboot.service, runs once)

resident world model: resident-world.timer regenerates /var/lib/resident/machine.md every 10 min (1 min after boot), records drift under intent #0 and drops events in /var/lib/resident/inbox/ for the resident agent
resident runtime: python3 + the resident CLI at /usr/lib/resident (symlinked as /usr/bin/{resident,intent,why}); RESIDENT_HOME=/var/lib/resident is set system-wide in /etc/environment

Resident agent identity: system user and group 'agent' (no password, nologin) owns /var/lib/resident; the observer units run as root (they must read all of /etc) with Group=agent so the state is shared with agentd/percept, which will run as this principal
Machine identity: /etc/machine-id is written at boot by resident-init from the persistent copy in /var/lib/dbus/machine-id (/etc is a tmpfs; identity lives in /var, never in the image)
Container network identity: /etc/hostname, /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf are bind-mounted by the container runtime (the VM image will use systemd-networkd + systemd-resolved instead)

Boot and service management: systemd as PID 1 (systemd, systemd-sysv), D-Bus system bus (dbus), journald, logind and the D-Bus-activated helpers (systemd-hostnamed/timedated/localed, woken by hostnamectl etc.); stock config under /etc/systemd and /etc/dbus-1
Console login on /dev/console: console-getty is systemd's default in containers (there are no ttys); harmless, will be replaced by the agent's own session in the VM image
TLS roots for outbound HTTPS from curl and python (ca-certificates; bundle at /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt, openssl defaults in /etc/ssl)
Network inspection: iproute2 (ss, ip) — the resident port collector shells out to ss
Process and memory inspection: procps (ps, free, uptime, sysctl) — used by the world model header
HTTP client for agents and intent --verify checks: curl
JSON tooling for shell pipelines and inbox/outbox events: jq
Periodic ext4 metadata scrub shipped by e2fsprogs (/etc/cron.d/e2scrub_all, /etc/e2scrub.conf); inert here because no cron daemon is installed and the root is read-only

Debian base system (essential + priority required/important): the minimal bookworm rootfs resident is built on; apt and dpkg are present but the root is read-only, so changes go through a new image, not apt-get
Dependencies auto-installed for the packages above (apt-mark showauto); see image/Dockerfile
Debian base configuration as shipped by the image's packages: /etc is an empty tmpfs at boot, populated from /usr/share/factory/etc by resident-init (config is a cache; the intent log is the truth)
